rules.title: Relocation Assistance for No-Fault Evictions under the RSO & JCO
rules.requirement: Landlords evicting for a no-fault reason in units covered by the RSO or JCO must file a Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD before serving notice, file a copy of the notice within 3 days, and pay relocation assistance within 15 days of the notice (or place it in escrow). Amounts depend on eligible/qualified status, tenancy length and income.
rules.key_value: Eligible household $11,000 (<3 yrs) / $14,400 (3+ yrs or low income); qualified household $23,150 / $27,400 (effective July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027)
rules.penalty: Failure to file the Landlord Declaration makes the eviction a violation of the RSO or JCO; non-payment may be raised as an affirmative defense by the tenant.
rules.status_basis: Amounts effective July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027; increase every July 1.

requires.name: rso_or_jco_covered
requires.text: units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause Ordinance (JCO)

exempt_if.name: resident_manager_replacement
exempt_if.text: Evicting a resident manager to replace him/her with another resident manager.

exempt_if.name: natural_disaster_hazard
exempt_if.text: required to evict due to hazardous conditions caused by a natural disaster, which is not caused by the landlord's negligence

coverage.summary: Applies to no-fault evictions from RSO or JCO covered units.
coverage.exemptions_summary: Exempt when replacing a resident manager or evicting due to natural disaster hazards not caused by landlord negligence; reduced amounts apply for Mom and Pop properties and single-family dwellings owned by natural persons.

rules.quoted_span:
All tenant not- at-fault evictions require payment of relocation assistance and the filing of a 
Declaration of Intent to Evict form with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) before 
evicting tenants from units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause 
Ordinance (JCO).

rules.title: Resident Protections Ordinance (RPO) relocation for demolition for new construction
rules.requirement: Landlords terminating tenancies of Protected Units to demolish for new construction must file with LAHD, serve notice, and pay relocation under the state Housing Crisis Act or city law, whichever is higher; lower income households receive enhanced standardized payments. Occupant protections include a right to remain up to 6 months, right to return and right of first refusal.
rules.key_value: Standardized payment: $115,480 extremely low, $96,750 very low, $87,450 low income (effective July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027)
rules.penalty: Financial penalties starting at $250,000 per displaced unit and withholding of LAHD permit clearances.
rules.status_basis: Bulletin states RPO adopted February 11, 2025 and effective 2/11/2025.

requires.name: protected_unit_demolition
requires.text: Protected Units that will be demolished for the purpose of new construction

coverage.summary: Applies to Protected Units (including all RSO units) demolished for new construction.

rules.quoted_span: Failure to comply with the RPO may result in financial penalties starting at $250,000 per displaced unit and withholding of LAHD permit clearances.
